knowledge:
- key_parameters: n_randomizations=Number of randomizations used to construct the error model for filtering random overlaps ;; MARGIN=Specifies whether to use "row", "col", or "both" dimensions for similarity metric evaluation ;; metric=Integer index representing the similarity metric to use (e.g., 4 for Fowlkes-Mallows index) ;; min_size=Minimum number of biclusters required in a Louvain community to be saved ;; row_threshold=Minimum frequency threshold (0 to 1) for a row element to be included in the final ensemble bicluster ;; col_threshold=Minimum frequency threshold (0 to 1) for a column element to be included in the final ensemble bicluster
- alternatives: Individual biclustering packages like fabia, isa2, biclust (for Plaid), and QUBIC. mosbi should be preferred when you want to combine multiple algorithms to obtain robust, consensus biclusters rather than relying on a single algorithm's output.
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing high-dimensional molecular profiling data (e.g., transcriptomics, metabolomics, lipidomics) where you expect overlapping groups of features to be co-regulated across subsets of samples.
- pitfalls: Individual biclustering algorithms may fail or throw errors on specific datasets; mosbi wrappers are designed to return empty lists in these cases to prevent workflow interruption. Additionally, setting row_threshold or col_threshold too high can lead to overly restrictive or empty ensemble biclusters.

workflows.name: ensemble_biclustering
workflows.intent: Run multiple biclustering algorithms on a data matrix, construct a similarity network with an error model, extract robust communities, and generate consensus ensemble biclusters.
input: data_matrix (A numeric matrix of normalized/z-scored molecular profiling data, with features as rows and samples as columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare and normalize data (log-transform and z-score) ;; 2. Run multiple biclustering algorithms (Fabia, ISA, Plaid, QUBIC) and combine results ;; 3. Compute a bicluster similarity network with an error model ;; 4. Extract Louvain communities of biclusters ;; 5. Generate consensus ensemble biclusters
workflows.code:
library(mosbi)

z_score <- function(x, margin = 2) {
    z_fun <- function(y) {
        (y - mean(y, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(y, na.rm = TRUE)
    }

    if (margin == 2) {
        return(apply(x, margin, z_fun))
    } else if (margin == 1) {
        return(t(apply(x, margin, z_fun)))
    }
}

bicluster_histo <- function(biclusters) {
    cols <- mosbi::colhistogram(biclusters)
    rows <- mosbi::rowhistogram(biclusters)

    graphics::par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
    hist(cols, main = "Column size ditribution")
    hist(rows, main = "Row size ditribution")
}

# get data
data(mouse_data)

mouse_data <- mouse_data[c(
    grep(
        "metabolite_identification",
        colnames(mouse_data)
    ),
    grep("^X", colnames(mouse_data))
)]

# Make data matrix
data_matrix <- z_score(log2(as.matrix(mouse_data[2:ncol(mouse_data)])), 1)

rownames(data_matrix) <- mouse_data$metabolite_identification

stats::heatmap(data_matrix)

# Fabia
fb <- mosbi::run_fabia(data_matrix) # In case the algorithms throws an error,
# return an empty list

# isa2
BCisa <- mosbi::run_isa(data_matrix)

# Plaid
BCplaid <- mosbi::run_plaid(data_matrix)

# QUBIC
BCqubic <- mosbi::run_qubic(data_matrix)

# Merge results of all algorithms
all_bics <- c(fb, BCisa, BCplaid, BCqubic)

bicluster_histo(all_bics)

bic_net <- mosbi::bicluster_network(all_bics, # List of biclusters
    data_matrix, # Data matrix
    n_randomizations = 5,
    # Number of randomizations for the
    # error model
    MARGIN = "both",
    # Use datapoints for metric evaluation
    metric = 4, # Fowlkes–Mallows index
    # For information about the metrics,
    # visit the "Similarity metrics
    # evaluation" vignette
    n_steps = 1000,
    # At how many steps should
    # the cut-of is evaluated
    plot_edge_dist = TRUE
    # Plot the evaluation of cut-off estimation
)

stats::heatmap(get_adjacency(bic_net))

plot(bic_net)

mosbi::plot_algo_network(bic_net, all_bics, vertex.label = NA)

# Prepare groups for plotting
weeks <- vapply(
    strsplit(colnames(data_matrix), "\\."),
    function(x) {
        return(x[1])
    }, ""
)

names(weeks) <- colnames(data_matrix)

print(sort(unique(weeks))) # 5 colors required

week_cols <- c("yellow", "orange", "red", "green", "brown")

# Plot network colored by week
mosbi::plot_piechart_bicluster_network(bic_net, all_bics, weeks,
    week_cols,
    vertex.label = NA
)
graphics::legend("topright",
    legend = sort(unique(weeks)),
    fill = week_cols, title = "Week"
)

coms <- mosbi::get_louvain_communities(bic_net,
    min_size = 3,
    bics = all_bics
)

ensemble_bicluster_list <- mosbi::ensemble_biclusters(coms, all_bics,
    data_matrix,
    row_threshold = .1,
    col_threshold = .1
)
